The given polar curve is the polar rose with $5$ petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is

$$
A=2{\int }_{-3\pi /20}^{\pi /20}{cos}^{2}⁡(5\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

The $1$st petal is traversed from ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{3\pi }{20}$ to ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{20},$ and the length of this interval is $\frac{\pi }{5}.$

To find the interval for the second petal, we have to add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the first petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{3} & ={\theta }_{1}+\frac{\pi }{5}=-\frac{3\pi }{20}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{20} \\ {\theta }_{4} & ={\theta }_{2}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{20}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, to obtain the interval for the third petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the second petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{5} & ={\theta }_{3}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{20}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {\theta }_{6} & ={\theta }_{4}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{9\pi }{20}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the interval for the fourth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the third petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{7} & ={\theta }_{5}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{9\pi }{20} \\ {\theta }_{8} & ={\theta }_{6}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{9\pi }{20}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{13\pi }{20}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the interval for the fifth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{5}$ to both ends of the interval of the fourth petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{9} & ={\theta }_{7}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{9\pi }{20}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{13\pi }{20} \\ {\theta }_{10} & ={\theta }_{8}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{13\pi }{20}+\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{17\pi }{20}\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, we obtain the following intervals for all $5$ petals of our rose:

$$
{{[-\frac{3\pi }{20},\frac{\pi }{20}]}_{⏟}}_{1\text{st}},\,{{[\frac{\pi }{20},\frac{\pi }{4}]}_{⏟}}_{2\text{nd}},\,{{[\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{9\pi }{20}]}_{⏟}}_{3\text{rd}},\,{{[\frac{9\pi }{20},\frac{13\pi }{20}]}_{⏟}}_{4\text{th}},\,{{[\frac{13\pi }{20},\frac{17\pi }{20}]}_{⏟}}_{5\text{th}}
$$

Therefore, the total area of the given polar curve can be obtained if the curve is traversed from $\theta =-\frac{3\pi }{10}$ to $\theta =\frac{17\pi }{20}:$

$$
{A}_{\text{total}}=2{\int }_{-3\pi /20}^{17\pi /20}{cos}^{2}⁡(5\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})\,\text{d}\theta 
$$
